minor.issue: Original seed deleted chef documents by email but left orphaned orders/menus/notifications under prior chefUUIDs. Because seeded orderIds (CF1001-CF1007) are reused across chefs, endpoints operating by orderId (accept/reject/request-delivery/delivery/acknowledge-postpone) resolved the OLDEST match and pushed side effects (dispatch, notifications) to a stale chef. Fixed in test iteration by extending force cleanup to also purge orders/menus/notifications for previous demo/newchef UUIDs and any lingering CF1001..CF1007 orderIds.

issues: Story auto-advances correctly; only cosmetic — the fancy legal-footer sits below the auth card and can be visually cropped on shorter viewports. Consider slightly smaller top spacing on the footer or making the card scroll within its column at <900px height.
Order-details-dialog, tracking-dialog, reject-dialog, otp-dialog trigger Radix a11y warning 'DialogContent requires a DialogTitle'. Add VisuallyHidden DialogTitle.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py: /api/orders/{id}/* endpoints resolve orders by orderId only (not chefUUID). In production, if the same orderId ever collides across chefs (as easily happens here between reseeds), operations will mutate the wrong record and push notifications to the wrong chef. Consider scoping by (chefUUID, orderId) or making orderId globally unique.
server.py is >800 lines now — split into routers (auth, files, menu, orders, notifications, revenue/payout, admin, seed) for maintainability.

rca of the issue: Seed race/dup-orderId: seed?force=true only removed chef documents for demo/newchef emails; orders/menus/notifications inserted under the prior chefUUIDs stayed in the DB. Since seed re-inserts CF1001..CF1007 with a new chefUUID, duplicates accumulated. All find_one({'orderId': ...}) queries then returned the OLDEST match. Impact: request-delivery/acknowledge-postpone/etc. mutated a stale chef's order and push_notification wrote to a chef with no live session. Mitigation applied in server.py seed endpoint: on force, also delete_many orders/menus/notifications for all previously-existing chefUUIDs for these emails, plus a defensive delete_many on the seeded orderId set.
